title: Navigating Uncertainty- Trend Following and Market Distortions - Systematic Investor - Ep.349

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Navigating Uncertainty- Trend Following and Market Distortions - Systematic Investor - Ep.349.docx

speakers: Mark Rzepczynski (caption: Mark Raspinski; systematic macro researcher and blogger)
summary: Systematic Investor 349 (May 2025): trend following's difficult 2025 with V-shaped reversals, state-created uncertainty and no follow-through, vol and leverage lessons, and why safe assets (Treasuries) proved fickle. Conclusion: trend remains a dynamic safe-asset substitute, but crisis alpha depends on crisis type.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: global supply chains drive overall demand. And that's sometimes missing in the whole discussion about tariffs and and trade
claims.claim: Modern trade rests on integrated global supply chains, so tariffs aimed at reshoring final-goods manufacturing cannot easily bring production back (Apple cannot build iPhones outside China), a headwind for tariff-driven policy aims.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you look at long-term inflation, there's a very high direct correlation to social trust and the faith that people have in institutions
claims.claim: Long-term inflation is inversely related to social trust in institutions (cited from Vincent Deluard on Jesse Felder's podcast), e.g. Switzerland has high trust and low inflation.
claims.testable: partly: needs a trust index versus inflation panel; causality unclear

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: he also talks about some of the low inflation periods in the 1950s in the US where social trust uh was pretty high
claims.claim: Low inflation in the 1950s coincided with high US trust in government, trust eroded in the 1970s and Volcker had to restore it, a historical analogy for trust and inflation.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: It's a interesting uh issue between correlation and causality
claims.claim: Trust is cultural (Anglo-Saxon systems show higher trust), so a trust-inflation link may be correlation not causality; a breakdown in trust with government could follow inflation or bad policy.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: all this financial engineering and more leverage ideas of products coming into the system
claims.claim: Leverage-based products (lending against Bitcoin on the assumption it compounds at 50%) add fragility, since most system breaks involve leverage.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: nothing compounds at 50% uh for an extended period of time
claims.claim: No asset can compound at 50% for an extended period, so extrapolating high past returns is unrealistic.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: We don't really like these uh V-shaped uh market moves and erratic uh reversals and there's been quite a few of them
claims.claim: Trend followers lose money in V-shaped markets and erratic reversals; the past 12 months had unusually many reversals across stocks, bonds and currencies and some long-lived managers saw their worst drawdowns.
claims.testable: yes: count sign flips versus trend return

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: nothing good happens below the 200 day moving average
claims.claim: The maxim that nothing good happens below the 200-day average was contradicted when stocks rose 9.5% in one day in April 2025 on a presidential call to buy; trend followers did not benefit.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: All crises are not the same and it's harder for us to generalize what the behavior will be in a given downturn in the stock market
claims.claim: Crisis alpha is not one-size-fits-all: trend following's payoff in a stock downturn depends on its length, its type and how fast the market comes back.
claims.indicator: trend return in equity drawdowns by type
claims.conditions: depends on drawdown speed and length
claims.testable: yes: classify drawdowns and compare trend returns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Btop 50 down 1.7% so far this month, down almost 5% for the for the year
claims.claim: Performance data to 28 May 2025: BTOP50 -5% YTD, SG CTA -8.5%, SG Trend -11.66%, STI -0.69%, versus MSCI World +3%, S&P 500 flat; Trend barometer 30.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend Index, Short-Term Traders Index

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: does trend work better in low vol environments?
claims.claim: A ChatGPT answer to a reader's question says trend performs better in rising or high-volatility periods (2008-09, 2014-15, 2020-22), tied to dislocations and regime changes.
claims.testable: yes: regress trend returns on VIX level and change

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: we need a certain level of volatility in which to uh identify trends and exploit trends
claims.claim: Trend following needs some volatility: extremely low volatility gives modest performance, higher volatility gives more dispersion and opportunity, but a volatility spike usually reverses trends and causes short-term losses.
claims.conditions: low vol: modest; high vol: opportunity; spikes: reversal losses
claims.testable: yes: bucket trend returns by vol level and vol change

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: periods of of of consolidation or even potential reversals vault tends to go up which is why it kind of makes sense uh to me at least that that's the time where dynamically you would reduce your risk
claims.claim: Volatility tends to rise around consolidation or reversal, so dynamic vol-based sizing reduces exposure just before give-back; long sustained trends can themselves occur in low vol.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: what's the V in Coco? How does that relate to the V in the S&P? It doesn't.
claims.claim: Volatility differs by market (cocoa vs S&P), so a single volatility regime across a multi-asset trend portfolio is not well defined.
claims.testable: yes: correlation of vols across markets

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: I just want to sort of make up for the lower V with higher leverage that that's a recipe for potential disaster
claims.claim: Raising leverage to hold volatility fixed after volatility falls (12 to 6) is a recipe for disaster if volatility reverses; leverage is the enemy.
claims.direction: reduce leverage rather than lever up

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: most experienced managers at least they will always have a flaw
claims.claim: Experienced managers set a floor on volatility estimates and look at long-term vol so they never take unbounded positions when vol collapses (e.g. short-rate contracts at zero rates).

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: this is the uncertainty that was created by the state as opposed to excesses in the market
claims.claim: 2025 uncertainty was created by the state (tariffs, man-made), unlike past crises built on market excesses like housing and tech bubbles; hence different behaviour from earlier trend-friendly crises.
claims.testable: partly: classification of crises is subjective

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: there are a number of of descriptors that we could use uh for uh markets and they have different implications on how a quant model and a trend model in particular will work
claims.claim: Market states can be described by risk (VIX), dispersion, correlation network, uncertainty indices and financial stress, each affecting trend models differently.
claims.testable: yes: condition trend returns on each descriptor

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: a spike in VIX or spike in volatility is good for trend following
claims.claim: A VIX spike is usually seen as good for trend following, but in 2025 the VIX spiked and fell back to about 18 without follow-through, so markets were not in a risk regime.
claims.indicator: VIX (level about 18, above 6-month average in April)
claims.testable: yes: trend payoff after VIX spikes with and without follow-through

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the CBOE has a dispersion index and
claims.claim: Dispersion (spread of returns across assets) is a state variable for trend opportunity; the CBOE dispersion index compares single-market volatility with the VIX.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: If there's less dispersion, then there's less opportunities to diversify and make money on trend following
claims.claim: Low cross-asset dispersion (one driver, here tariffs) reduces diversification and trend profit; dispersion rose in 2025 but not to an extreme.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the network has become very tight in in earlier in April
claims.claim: The correlation or causal network across markets tightened in April 2025 because everything was driven by the tariff theme and loosened afterwards.
claims.testable: yes: average pairwise correlation versus trend returns

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: we have a monetary policy uh uncertainty index. We have tariff uh uncertainty indices
claims.claim: Newspaper word-count uncertainty indices (monetary policy, tariff, global) were elevated in early 2025, trade uncertainty off the charts and still elevated.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: that can explain why there's been more of a flow of capital to Europe than relative to the United States
claims.claim: US policy uncertainty above Europe's explains capital flowing to Europe from the US.
claims.testable: partly: flow data versus uncertainty index

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: stress is elevated, but it's still nowhere near what we saw in 2020 or 2008
claims.claim: Financial stress indices (ECB, banks, St. Louis Fed) were elevated but far below 2020 and 2008, so not a systemic crisis environment.
claims.indicator: ECB / St. Louis Fed financial stress indices

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: Most times when we've thought about crisis and where trend following has made money has been when there's been uncertainty but then the resolution was something that was negative
claims.claim: Trend profits when uncertainty is resolved negatively; in 2025 uncertainty was resolved positively (tariff relief), causing a sharp reversal in markets and in trend positions.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there's no follow through, right? That's that's kind of what what what is missing here.
claims.claim: 2025 sell-offs were reversals without follow-through, like March 2020, where central bank stepped in and trend followers positioned for a further sell-off that never came.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: they're man-made events which means is that they could be turned on and turned off fairly quickly
claims.claim: Man-made crises (lockdowns, tariffs) can be turned on and off quickly; trend following needs a slow behavioural response from investors that fast policy responses prevent.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: this is what's preventing markets from followrough. It is intervention by politicians uh or or central banks
claims.claim: Political and central bank intervention (stimulus, tariff pauses, calls to buy) prevents follow-through in markets and makes trend environments difficult.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: trend following is not the first responder
claims.claim: Trend following is a second responder: it only pays if a crisis turns out much bigger than a brief shock.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: It's long long volatility but it's short short volatility
claims.claim: Trend following is long long-term volatility (dispersion of returns) but short short-term volatility because stops get hit on large short-term moves, like a knock-out option.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: I'm going to be have stops intraday if you have a large intraday move then it's a more likelihood I could get stopped out and then the uh the market closes above whatever my moving average could be
claims.claim: Intraday stops can trigger on large intraday moves even when the close returns above the moving average, costing longer-term trend followers positions.
claims.testable: yes: stop-out frequency intraday vs close

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we need to be longer term but we also
claims.claim: Trend followers face a tension between longer lookbacks (better in data) and fast reaction for risk control, handled via multiple time frames or other methods.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: if you make a mistake on execution with your long-term trend model, it's may take you a long time before you can reverse that
claims.claim: Execution matters most to short-term traders, but a long-term model's execution error persists for a long time.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: bonds were not really a safe asset during this period at all
claims.claim: Stocks and bonds hedge each other only when negatively correlated; in April-May 2025 bonds fell with stocks (30y above 5%, 10y above 4.5%), so Treasuries gave no safety.
claims.testable: yes: bond returns in equity drawdowns

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: We're still going to have high deficits
claims.claim: High US deficits after the budget bill risk a bond-vigilante repricing like the UK trust moment, so safe assets need rethinking.
claims.testable: partly: yield response to deficit news

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: in 1925 the UK was considered the premier economy
claims.claim: Historical analogy: UK sterling was top currency in 1925 yet the IMF bailed out the UK in 1975, showing reserve status can erode within 50 years.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we're in the 40-year cycle now where interest rates are going higher
claims.claim: Rates are in the early phase of a 40-year upward cycle, and heavy fixed-income allocations (40% US, 60-80% Europe) look too high; US default risk is no longer zero.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: a safe asset is one that has low correlation and negative correlation when uh markets are down
claims.claim: Empirical definition: a safe asset has low or negative correlation when markets fall; a hedge asset differs; Treasuries and bills can become a fickle safe asset.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: It does very well during tariff and uh tariff periods
claims.claim: Gold works as a safe asset in tariff-uncertainty crises but not in others (recent paper); T-bills fail during inflation.
claims.testable: yes: gold returns by crisis type

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the dynamic characteristics may mean that if we go into an extended period of un uh where traditional safe assets are no longer safe
claims.claim: Trend following was also fickle in April-May 2025, but its long-short dynamic characteristic may give safety in extended periods when traditional safe assets fail.
claims.indicator: trend returns when bonds fall with stocks
claims.testable: yes: trend returns when stock-bond correlation positive

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it's one you can stick with because you're comfortable with the process of the investment
claims.claim: A great investment is one you can stick with because you understand its process; trend following is rational, adaptive, long-short and globally diversified.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Bergkshire haways have had three or four draw downs over the years of more
claims.claim: Berkshire Hathaway had three or four drawdowns over 50%; 20-25% corrections are not worth worrying about, judge strategies over 10-40 years, as with trend following.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: the concept of a safe asset is dynamic
claims.claim: The safe-asset status of Treasury bills depends on issuer behaviour and changes over time, so substitutes such as trend following can serve as safe haven.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: riding bubbles can be a strategy
claims.claim: Trend following is valuation agnostic: it can ride overvalued markets in bubbles as well as undervalued ones.

claims.speaker: Mark Rzepczynski
claims.quote: momentum and carry which we've been probably talking about for years and years
claims.claim: Recent machine-learning work on currency trading finds momentum and carry the two most important features across all models.
